name: Grade 6 T2: mBot Loops, Sensors, and Challenges
description: Loops, repeated patterns, sensors, conditions, if/then logic, route maps, challenge goals, and success rules.

words.definition: To do the same action again.
words.example: The robot repeated the turn command four times.

words.definition: A programming structure that repeats instructions.
words.example: A loop made the square movement program shorter.

words.definition: A repeated design, action, or sequence.
words.example: The robot followed a forward-turn pattern.

words.definition: A shape with four equal sides and four corners.
words.example: The mBot used a loop to drive in a square.

words.definition: A path that moves back and forth in sharp turns.
words.example: The robot followed a zigzag path between markers.

words.definition: A part that detects something, such as a line, object, light, or distance.
words.example: The sensor detected an obstacle in front of the robot.

words.definition: To notice or sense something.
words.example: The line sensor can detect dark tape.

words.definition: Something in the way that a robot may need to avoid.
words.example: The mBot stopped when it detected an obstacle.

words.definition: A mark or path that a robot sensor can follow or detect.
words.example: The robot used the black line as a guide.

words.definition: Information a computer or robot receives.
words.example: A sensor value is an input.

words.definition: What a robot or program does after an input or condition.
words.example: The response was to stop and play a sound.

words.definition: A rule or test that can be true or false.
words.example: The condition checked whether an obstacle was close.

words.definition: A programming word used to start a condition.
words.example: If the robot sees a line, then it turns.

words.definition: A programming word that introduces what happens when a condition is true.
words.example: If the sensor detects an obstacle, then the robot stops.

words.definition: A condition result that means the rule is met.
words.example: The condition was true when the object was close.

words.definition: A condition result that means the rule is not met.
words.example: The condition was false when no obstacle was detected.

words.definition: A diagram that shows steps, choices, and results in a process.
words.example: The flowchart showed the sensor condition and two responses.

words.definition: A drawing that shows the path and movement steps a robot should follow.
words.example: The route map labeled every turn and stop point.

words.definition: A task that asks students to solve a problem or meet a goal.
words.example: The final challenge required movement plus one sensor.

words.definition: The result a person or robot is trying to achieve.
words.example: The goal was for the robot to stop before the obstacle.

words.definition: A clear way to decide whether a challenge worked.
words.example: The success rule was that the robot must finish inside the taped box.

words.definition: A class area or activity spot used to practice a skill.
words.example: One station practiced sensor testing.

words.definition: Able to act using a program without being controlled step by step by a person.
words.example: The autonomous robot reacted when it detected a line.

words.definition: To look for the cause of a problem and try possible fixes.
words.example: The team had to troubleshoot the sensor response.
